subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should OpenClaw keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines as non-deliverable examples and add a warning, or should it extract valid fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: extraction reduces missed attachments but changes the code-fence safety contract, while warn-only preserves current behavior and makes the failure diagnosable.

options.title: Land warn-only behavior
options.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines visible and non-deliverable, but emit a delivery-boundary warning so users can diagnose the mistake.

options.title: Extract fenced tokens
options.body: Treat standalone valid `MEDIA:` lines inside fences as attachments, accepting the risk that examples can trigger delivery.

options.title: Document only
options.body: Keep runtime unchanged and rely on docs/prompt guidance, leaving the failure silent in logs.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only behavior
recommendation.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines visible and non-deliverable, but emit a delivery-boundary warning so users can diagnose the mistake.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has repeated history on the media parser and user-facing media guidance, making him the best available owner for the product contract choice.
